title: Air pressure: a tin box crushed from every side (বাতাসের চাপ)
placement: Book page 142–143, topic 5.4 (বাতাসের চাপ): next to চিত্র ৫.০৭ (a tin box (a) emptied of air by a pump: (b) what would happen if air pressed only from the top, flattened; (c) what really happens, crushed from every side) and the paragraphs before it: the air column over 1 m² (চিত্র ৫.০৬, 10⁵ N/m², about an elephant's weight), 'চাপ ভেক্টর নয়, তার কোনো দিক নেই তাই যেকোনো জায়গায় চারদিকে চাপ সমান', and why we don't feel the air's pressure (and astronauts wear pressure suits).
description: Air pressure (page 142, topic 5.4), decluttered: one clear tin on a plain table, a soft floor and a gentle sky, nothing else. The tin box, a cube 10 cm on a side (as the book's চিত্র ৫.০৭), is plain silver with a slate band. One outlined red arrow presses in on each open face (the air's 1,00,000 Pa = 10⁵ N/m², the same everywhere); on the left face a blue arrow beside it pushes out (the air inside) just as hard. Each tap of the big button pumps air out (20,000 Pa a stroke, made simple, said in the panel): the blue arrow shrinks, the red ones stay, and the tin buckles in from every side while the camera leans in. The panel lists the outside and inside pressure and works out the force left over on one face, F = (P outside − P inside) × A with A = 0.01 m² (up to 1,000 N). After five strokes the book's contrast: 'what if air pushed only from the top?' shows the box as a pale ghost flattening (চিত্র ৫.০৭ b, marked as imagined), and 'what really happens' replays the crush from every side (c). The row of words also goes to the air column (চিত্র ৫.০৬): a see-through 1 m × 1 m column whose weight, 10⁵ N, is shown beside an elephant's (P = F/A = 10⁵ N/m²); and to our body: a student with three red arrows pressing in and equal blue arrows pushing out (they cancel); in space only the inside arrows are left (why astronauts wear pressure suits). Test tab: 5 questions with a note for every wrong choice. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
